name: 3% saline
Dose: Oral: 0.5 - 1ml per feed, serve with feeding  Severe hyponatraemia < 120 mmol/L or symptomatic hyponatraemia  IV: 3-5mL/kg of 3% saline administered within 15 minutes (This will raise serum sodium 2.5-4mmol/L)  Note: Hypertonic solution, Osmolarity: 1027 mOsm/L 1ml= 0.5mmol sodium Sodium deficit calculation: Deficit in mmol = (desired sodium - serum sodium) x 0.6 **Overly rapid correction of severe hyponatremia can result in osmotic demyelination**
Incompatibilities: Fat emulsion

name: Acetazolamide 250mg Tablet
Dose: 5-10mg/kg BD-QID TB hydrocephalus: 25-50mg/kg TDS-QID, usual dose: 100mg/kg/day (in divided doses)
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Strength of EXTEMP prep: 25mg/mL

name: Acetylcysteine 200mg/ml Injection [NAC]
Dose: PCM toxicity: Step 1: 200mg/kg in 3mL/kg D5, infuse over 4 hours. Step 2: 100mg/kg in 7mL/kg D5, infuse over 16 hours. May repeat Step 2 if clinically indicated. Acute liver failure: Step 1: 150mg/kg in 50mL D5 loading dose, infuse over 1-2 hours. Step 2: 150mg/kg in 50mL D5 infuse over 24 hours.

name: Acetylsalicylic acid/ (Aspirin) 300mg tablet
Dose: Neonate: Antiplatelet effect; post operative congenital heart repair or recurrent arterial ischemic stroke: 1-5 mg/kg OD. Serve after feeding.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare, ensure well mixing, watchout for sedimentation.

name: Actrapid 1000 iu/10ml (Insulin) injection
Dose: Hyperglycemia: Full strength dilution 2 units/kg in 20ml NS (1ml/H=0.1 unit/kg/H). Half strength 1 unit/kg in 20ml NS (1ml/H=0.05 unit/kg/H). Quarter strength 0.5 unit/kg in 20ml NS (1ml/H=0.025 unit/kg/H). Hyperkalemia: Glucose-insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 U/kg insulin in 5mL/kg D10% IV over 1 hour, check glucose to ensure no hypoglycemia.
Incompatibilities: Cefoperazone, Diazepam, Ketamine, Micafungin, Phenytoin, Tazocin, Polymyxin B, Protamine sulphate, Rocuronium, Bactrim
Method of administration: Hyperglycemia: continuous infusion. Hyperkalemia: infusion over 1 hour.

name: Adenosine 6mg/2ml injection
Dose: 1st dose 0.1mg/kg/dose. If no response within 2 min, give 2nd dose 0.2mg/kg/dose. If no response, give 3rd dose 0.3mg/kg/dose. Max 0.3mg/kg/dose.
Incompatibilities: Single line, do not mix with other medications
Method of administration: IV push over 1-2 sec followed by rapid NS flush via 3-way tap, prefer upper limb close to heart

name: Adrenaline 1mg/1ml (1:1000) injection
Dose: Cardiac arrest: IV 0.2ml/kg of 1:10,000 (0.01-0.03mg/kg). ET: 1mL/kg of 1:10,000. Anaphylaxis IM: 0.01mg/kg/dose (max 0.3mg). Continuous infusion: dilution 0.3mg/kg in 50ml D5%/NS (1ml/hr=0.1mcg/kg/min), initial 0.02-0.1mcg/kg/min, usual range 0.05-0.5mcg/kg/min, max 1mcg/kg/min. Nebulisation croup: 0.5ml/kg of 1:1000 (max 5ml) diluted in 4ml NS, may repeat q20min.
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Ampicillin, Micafungin, Omeprazole, Sodium bicarbonate, Thiopenthal
Method of administration: Rapid push+3ml saline flush, or ETT, or continuous infusion, or nebulisation

name: Alphacalcidol drops 2 mcg/ml
Dose: Neonates: 0.1 microgram/kg OD. Child >1 month <20kg: 0.05 microgram/kg OD. 1 drop=0.1 microgram.

name: Alprostadil 500mcg/ml injection (Prostin)
Dose: Maintain patency of ductus arteriosus: 3microgram/kg in 50ml NS or D5%, 1ml/hr=1ng/kg/min. Apnoea/hypotension may occur at higher doses.
Incompatibilities: Levofloxacin, lipid
Storage after reconstitution: Fridge 14 days (pure); after dilution 24 hours, change infusion syringe every 24h

name: Amikacin 250mg/2ml injection
Dose: Based on CGA: <30 weeks 15mg/kg stat, MD 7.5mg/kg 24h. 30 to <35 weeks 15mg/kg stat, MD 10mg/kg 24h. >=35 weeks to term <1 week 15mg/kg 24h. Term >=1 week 25mg/kg stat, 18mg/kg 24h.
Incompatibilities: Lipid, Amphothericin B, Ampicillin, Azithromycin, Diazepam, Ganciclovir, Heparin >1u/ml, Insulin, Imipenem/Cilastatin, Phenytoin, Propofol, Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole, Thiopental
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour; TDM 2nd dose post2 & post6 levels if OD dosing

name: Aminophyline 250mg/10ml injection
Dose: Apnea of prematurity: Loading 5mg/kg over 1h, maintenance 2-6mg/kg/day q12h starting 12h after loading. Acute severe bronchospasm: loading 10mg/kg over 1h, maintenance by age.
Incompatibilities: Amiodarone, Cefepime, Ceftriaxone, Cefotaxime, Ciprofloxacin, Clindamycin, Dobutamine, Epinephrine, Hydralazine, Insulin, Methylprednisolone, Morphine, C-penicillin, Phenytoin, Vancomycin

name: Amiodarone 150mg/3ml injection
Dose: SVT/JET Loading: 15mg/kg in 50ml D5% at 5ml/hr (25mcg/kg/min) for 4h, then maintenance 1-3ml/hr (5-15mcg/kg/min, max 1.2g/day). Pulseless VF/VT (CPR): 5mg/kg (max 300mg) rapid bolus, repeat twice to max 15mg/kg. VF/VT: Loading 5mg/kg over 1h, maintenance 5-25mcg/kg/min.
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Ampicillin, Ceftazidime, Cefazolin, Digoxin, Heparin, Imipenem-Cilastatin, Micafungin, Tazocin, Sodium bicarbonate, PN, lipid

name: Amoxicillin & Clavulanic acid 1.2g injection (Augmentin)
Dose: 1st week of life: 60mg/kg 12 hourly. After 1st week: 60mg/kg 8 hourly. Dose is amoxicillin+clavulanic acid combined.
Incompatibilities: Glucose 5%/10%, sodium bicarbonate, PN, lipid emulsion, blood products, amiodarone, amikacin, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, hydrocortisone, methylprednisolone, midazolam, metronidazole

name: Amoxicillin trihydrate 125mg/5ml syrup
Dose: ORAL 25-30mg/kg BD. UTI prophylaxis 10-15mg/kg OD. Asplenia 20mg/kg OD.

name: Amphothericin B 50mg (conventional) injection
Dose: Systemic fungal infection: 1mg/kg 24h for 14 days, may increase to 1.5mg/kg max.
Incompatibilities: Single line, do not mix with other medications
Method of administration: IV infusion over 6 hours, single line; rapid infusion can cause CVS collapse

name: Ampicillin 1g & Sulbactam 0.5g injection (Unasyn)
Dose: Neonate <=7 days: IV 75mg/kg 12 hourly. >8 days: IV 75mg/kg 6 hourly. MDR ABA: <1mo 75mg/kg 6h; >=1mo 150mg/kg 6h.
Incompatibilities: Amiodarone, Ciprofloxacin
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30 mins; 3 hours for severe/MDR infections

name: Ampicillin 500mg injection
Dose: General: 1st week IV 50mg/kg 12 hourly. >1 week IV 50mg/kg 6 hourly. GBS meningitis: PNA<=7d 100mg/kg 8h; PNA8-60d 75mg/kg 6h.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Amiodarone, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Adrenaline, Erythromycin lactobionate, Fluconazole, Gentamicin, Hydralazine, Metoclopramide, Midazolam, Nicardipine, PN, Lipid, Sodium bicarbonate
Ref: Neofax, leaflet, ANMF, Queensland Clinical Guideline

name: Arginine 5g/sachet
Dose: Consult Metabolic/Genetic specialist first. CPS/OTC/NAGS deficiency: Oral 170mg/kg/day in 3-4 doses. ASL/ASS/citrullinemia: Oral 400-700mg/kg/day in 3-4 doses.

name: Atropine 1mg/ml injection
Dose: Bradycardia: IV 0.01-0.02mg/kg over 1 min, repeat q10-15min, max 0.5mg/dose. ET: 0.04-0.06mg/kg. Intubation: IV/IM 0.01mg/kg. Preanaesthetic: PO 0.02mg/kg 1h before induction.
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, Ampicillin, Heparin, Sodium bicarbonate, Thiopentone

name: Azithromycin 500mg injection
Dose: Pertussis: <6mo 10mg/kg OD x5d. Ureaplasma eradication preterm: 20mg/kg OD IV x3d. Chlamydia/mycoplasma pneumonia: 10mg/kg IV OD day1-2 then step down oral.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Cefotaxime, Ceftazidime, Ceftriaxone, Cefuroxime, Clindamycin, Fentanyl, Frusemide, Gentamicin, Imipenem-Cilastatin, Morphine, Piperacillin-Tazobactam, Potassium chloride

name: Benzathine Penicillin G 2.4 MIU injection
Dose: Congenital syphilis (defaulting risk): IM 50,000 u/kg single dose.

name: Beractant intratracheal suspension 8ml
Dose: Intratracheal 4ml/kg/dose, max 8ml

name: C-penicillin/ Penicillin G/ Benzylpenicillin 1 MU injection
Dose: General: 1st week 100,000 unit/kg 12 hourly; after 1st week 100,000 unit/kg 6 hourly. Congenital syphilis: PNA<=7d 50,000u/kg 12h (->8h dosing at PNA8d); PNA8-28d 50,000u/kg 8h; PNA>=29d 50,000u/kg 6h. Meningitis/GBS: PNA<=7d 150,000u/kg 8h; PNA8-28d 150,000u/kg 6h; infants 100,000u/kg 6h.
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Amphoterin B, Dobutamine, Erythromycin, Ganciclovir, Heparin, Metoclopramide, Netilmicin, Noradrenaline, Phenobarbitone, Phenytoin, Potassium chloride, Protamine sulphate, Thiopentone, Tranexamic acid
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30 minutes; separate from aminoglycoside with a flush (penicillins inactivate aminoglycosides)

name: Caffeine citrate 20mg/ml injection
Dose: CAUTION: Caffeine citrate 2mg = caffeine base 1mg. PRESCRIBE IN CAFFEINE BASE. Loading: IV 10 mg/kg (base) stat. Maintenance: 1st week of life 2.5 mg/kg 24h; week2 3 mg/kg 24h; week3-4 3.5 mg/kg 24h; week5-8 4 mg/kg 24h. Max 10 mg/kg 24h. Switch to oral once feeds reach >=100ml/kg/day.
Incompatibilities: Aciclovir, adenosine, furosemide, pantoprazole
Ref: Leaflet, NeoFax, UpToDate, Canterbury DHB, KEMH, ANMF 2022

name: Caffeine citrate 20mg/ml oral solution
Dose: Prescribe in caffeine BASE (20mg/ml = 10mg/ml base). Maintenance: week1 2.5mg/kg 24h; week2 3mg/kg 24h; week3-4 3.5mg/kg 24h; week5-8 4mg/kg 24h. Max 10mg/kg 24h. May oralise once feeds >=100ml/kg/day.

name: Calcium gluconate 10% (1g/10ml) injection
Dose: Fast correction: 0.5ml/kg/dose over 60 minutes. Continuous infusion for symptomatic hypocalcemia: 10-33mg/kg/hour. 1ml contains 94mg calcium gluconate = 0.23mmol Ca2+.
Incompatibilities: PN, lipids, Amphotericin, Ceftriaxone, Clindamycin, Dobutamine, Digoxin, Fluconazole, Phosphate, Sodium Bicarbonate
Method of administration: IV bolus slowly over 60 min, not exceeding 100mg/min; via central line whenever possible

name: Calcium Polystyrene Sulphonate Powder (Kalimate)
Dose: PR for hyperkalemia: 0.3-0.6g/kg/dose PRN or q6-12h. 1g/kg exchanges approx 1.6mmol K+. SHOULD NOT BE GIVEN ORALLY in neonates due to reduced gut motility - PR only, retain >=30 min, evacuate 8-12h later.

name: Cefazolin Sodium 1g Injection
Dose: Ward practice: 50mg/kg/dose 8H, up to 6H in severe infection. Surgical prophylaxis: 30mg/kg, up to 50mg/kg high-risk surgery.

name: Cefepime 1g injection
Dose: <=28 days PNA 50mg/kg 12 hourly. >28 days PNA 50mg/kg 8 hourly.
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Aminophylline, Amphotericin B, Diazepam, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Erythromycin lactobionate, Ganciclovir, Magnesium sulphate, Metoclopramide, Midazolam, Morphine, Nicardipine, Phenytoin, Vancomycin

name: Cefotaxime 1g injection
Dose: Sepsis: PNA0-7d 50mg/kg 12h; PNA8-28d 50mg/kg 8h; PNA>28d 50mg/kg 6h. Meningitis: <=1wk 50mg/kg 8h; >1wk 50mg/kg 6h. Ophthalmia neonatorum: IV 100mg/kg single dose.
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Fluconazole, Protamine sulphate, Sodium bicarbonate, Vancomycin

name: Ceftazidime 1g injection
Dose: 0-7 days 50mg/kg 12h. 8-28 days 50mg/kg 8h. >28 days 50mg/kg 6h. Melioidosis 50mg/kg 6h over 3h.
Incompatibilities: Amiodarone, Azithromycin, Erythromycin lactobionate, Fluconazole, Midazolam, Phenytoin, Nicardipine, Vancomycin

name: Ceftriaxone 1g injection
Dose: Meningitis >=29 days age: 50mg/kg 12h. Other infections: 50mg/kg 24h. AVOID USE IN NEONATES DUE TO RISK OF KERNICTERUS.
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Azithromycin, Calcium gluconate, Fluconazole, Vancomycin

name: Cefuroxime 750mg injection
Dose: <7 days 50mg/kg 12h. 7-21 days 50mg/kg 8h. 21-28 days 50mg/kg 6-8h.
Incompatibilities: Clarithromycin, fluconazole, gentamicin, midazolam, sodium bicarbonate, vancomycin

name: Cloxacillin 500mg injection
Dose: <=7 days: 50mg/kg 12H. Day8-28: 50mg/kg 8H. Infants/children: 50mg/kg 6H, up to 4H in severe infection.
Incompatibilities: Gentamicin, lipids, pantoprazole, morphine

name: Colistin (Polymyxin E) 1 MIU injection
Dose: Neb for MDR Acinetobacter VAP: colistin base 4mg/kg 12h up to 14 days. IV: Load 200,000 unit/kg over 30 min, then 200,000 unit/kg/day in 3 divided doses.

name: Dexamethasone 8mg/2ml injection
Dose: Low dose DART: 0.075mg/kg BD x3d, 0.05mg/kg BD x3d, 0.025mg/kg BD x2d, 0.01mg/kg BD x2d then off. Moderate dose (term CLD, ANMF 2022): 0.25mg/kg 12h x3d, 0.15mg/kg 12h x3d, 0.1mg/kg 12h x3d, 0.05mg/kg 12h x3d, 0.025mg/kg 12h x6d then off. Post-extubation stridor: 0.25mg/kg 8h x3 doses starting 4-12h pre-extubation. Croup: 0.3-0.6mg/kg stat.
Incompatibilities: Glycopyrrolate, Midazolam, Vancomycin
Ref: Leaflet, KEMH, Neomed, Paed Protocol 4th ed

name: Dexmedetomidine HCl 100mcg/mL Injection
Dose: CONTRAINDICATED in heart block/severe ventricular dysfunction. <37w GA: loading 0.2mcg/kg over 15min (if needed), maintenance 0.2mcg/kg/hr, max 1mcg/kg/hr. Term <=14d: loading 0.35mcg/kg, maintenance 0.3mcg/kg/hr, max 1.2mcg/kg/hr. Term >14d: loading 0.5mcg/kg, maintenance 0.5-0.75mcg/kg/hr, max 1.5mcg/kg/hr. NOT FOR IV RESCUE BOLUS.
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin B forms, diazepam, ketamine, pantoprazole, phenytoin

name: Dobutamine 250mg/20ml injection
Dose: Dilution: 30mg/kg in 50ml D5%/NS (1ml/hr=10mcg/kg/min). Low dose 2.5mcg/kg/min minimal hemodynamic effect. Moderate 5-7.5mcg/kg/min increases CO. Higher 5-20mcg/kg/min increases CO and BP.
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Aminophylline, Cefepime, Bumetanide, Diazepam, Digoxin, Frusemide, Micafungin, Phenytoin, Tazocin, Sodium bicarbonate

name: Dopamine 200mg/5ml injection
Dose: Dilution: 30mg/kg in 50ml D5%/NS (1ml/hr=10mcg/kg/min). Low 1-5mcg/kg/min - renal blood flow. Intermediate 5-10mcg/kg/min - CO+BP. High 10-20mcg/kg/min - vasoconstriction.
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Amphotericin B, Ampicillin, Cefepime, Frusemide, Insulin, Penicillin G, Sodium bicarbonate

name: Fentanyl citrate 0.1mg/2ml injection
Dose: Sedation/analgesia bolus: 0.5-4mcg/kg over 3-5min, may repeat q2-4h. Continuous infusion: 1-5mcg/kg/hr (start 1mcg/kg/hr). Pre-med for intubation: 2-4mcg/kg bolus, wait >=3min for onset.
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Pantoprazole, Phenytoin, Thiopentone, Bactrim

name: Fluconazole 100mg/50ml injection
Dose: Loading: IV 25mg/kg stat. Maintenance: IV 12mg/kg 24h. Prophylaxis (high risk following Candida sepsis treatment): 6mg/kg twice weekly.
Incompatibilities: Ampicillin, calcium gluconate, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, clindamycin, digoxin, frusemide, imipenem-cilastatin, pentamidine

name: Gentamicin 80mg/2ml injection
Dose: <29 GA weeks: <1wk 5mg/kg 48h; 8-28d 4mg/kg 36h; >=29d 4mg/kg 24h. 30-34 GA weeks: <1wk 4.5mg/kg 36h; >=1wk 4mg/kg 24h. >=35 GA weeks: 4mg/kg 24h.
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin B, Ampicillin, Azithromycin, Frusemide, Imipenem/Cilastatin, Heparin >1u/ml, Indomethacin, Propofol

name: Glucagon 1mg/ml injection
Dose: Persistent hypoglycemia: 0.5-1mg stat IV/IM/SC, then IVI 5-10mcg/kg/hr (dilution 0.25mg/kg in 25ml D10%, 1ml/hr=10mcg/kg/hr).
Incompatibilities: Solutions containing calcium

name: Heparin 25,000 IU/5ml injection
Dose: Maintaining CVL patency: 0.5-1ml/hr. Thrombosis/PE treatment: loading 75unit/kg over 10min, then 20-30 unit/kg/hr, adjust by APTT. Heparin lock: 10 units/mL, 0.5-1mL per lumen.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Amiodarone, Caspofungin, Diazepam, Gentamicin, Netilmicin, Phenytoin, Vancomycin

name: Human Albumin 20% injection
Dose: 5 ml/kg
Diluent: NS, D5, D10, 0.45% NaCl, D5NS. DO NOT dilute with WFI (haemolysis risk)
Incompatibilities: TPN, Lipid, Micafungin, Midazolam, Vancomycin, Verapamil

name: Hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100mg injection
Dose: Persistent hypoglycemia: IV 1-2mg/kg 12h or 8h, or 1mg/kg 6h refractory. CAH: 10-15mg/m2/day in 3 doses (up to 20mg/m2/day initial). Early neonatal hypotension: IV 2mg/kg stat then 1mg/kg 8-12h. Anti-inflammatory: 2.5mg/kg 6h. Acute asthma: 4mg/kg 6h (max 100mg).
Incompatibilities: Frusemide, Midazolam, Phenobarbital, Phenytoin

name: Imipenem & Cilastatin 500mg/500mg injection
Dose: Dose based on imipenem component: 1st week 25mg/kg 12h. After 1st week 25mg/kg 8h.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Amiodarone, Azithromycin, Fluconazole, Gentamicin, Lorazepam, Milrinone, Sodium bicarbonate

name: L-arginine 5g/10ml injection
Dose: Hyperammonemia (urea cycle defect) anti-ammonia cocktail: IV 250 mg/kg. Mix with sodium benzoate 250mg/kg and sodium phenylbutyrate 250mg/kg in D10% total 50ml infuse over 90 min (33ml/hr). Maintenance: same dilution infuse over 24 hours.
Incompatibilities: Single line, only mixable with sodium benzoate & sodium phenylbutyrate
Method of administration: IV infusion via large vein/central line

name: Levetiracetam 500mg/5ml injection
Dose: Seizure loading: IV 40mg/kg stat. Maintenance: 20mg/kg/dose 12h up to 60mg/kg/day max (Paeds Protocol). ANMF alt: loading 40mg/kg + additional 20mg/kg after 30min if needed; maintenance 10mg/kg 8h starting 12h after loading, up to 30mg/kg/dose (max 60mg/kg/day).
Ref: Leaflet, NeoFax, Leeds Teaching Hospital, Paed protocol, ANMF

name: Magnesium sulphate 2.465g/5ml injection
Dose: Hypomagnesemia: 0.1mL/kg (50mg/kg) over 4 hours. PPHN loading (if required): 50mg/kg over 30min then maintenance 30mg/kg/hr (dilute 1 vial 2.47g in 25ml NS, run 0.3ml/kg/hr). Torsades/VT: 25-50mg/kg IV. Bronchospasm: 50mg/kg loading then 30mg/kg/hr maintenance.
Incompatibilities: Lipid, Amiodarone, Amphothericin B, Calcium chloride, Cefepime, Pantoprazole, Sodium bicarbonate
Method of administration: IV infusion over 4 hours, max rate 0.04mmol/kg/min

name: Meropenem 500mg injection
Dose: 1st week of life: 40mg/kg 12 hourly. After 1st week: 40mg/kg 8 hourly. Severe infection continuous: 120mg/kg/day divided into 6 doses, infuse over 4h. Renal adjust by eGFR.
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Amphotericin B, calcium gluconate, Metronidazole, sodium bicarbonate, Zidovudine

name: Metronidazole 500mg/100ml injection
Dose: Loading: 15mg/kg stat. Maintenance: 0-28 days 7.5mg/kg 12h; >28 days 7.5mg/kg 8h. <2kg start maintenance after 48h; >2kg after 24h.
Incompatibilities: Meropenem

name: Midazolam 5mg/1ml, 5mg/5ml injection
Dose: Bolus: 0.1-0.2mg/kg, up to 0.5mg/kg. Continuous infusion: 3mg/kg in 50ml NS, dose range 1-4mcg/kg/min (higher in ICU). Administer slow over 2-5min, NOT rapid bolus (hypotension/seizure risk).
Incompatibilities: Lipids, Acyclovir, Albumin, Aminophylline, Amoxicillin, Ampicillin, Azithromycin, Cefepime, Ceftazidime, Dexamethasone, Ertapenem, Esomeprazole, Cloxacillin, Frusemide, Ganciclovir, Hydrocortisone sodium succinate, Imipenem-cilastatin, Omeprazole, Phenobarbitone, Piperacillin-tazobactam, Sodium bicarbonate, Thiopentone, Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole

name: Milrinone 10mg/10ml injection
Dose: Loading (usually omitted): 1.5mg/kg in 50ml D5%, 2.5ml over 1h (75mcg/kg). Maintenance: 1.5mg/kg in 50ml D5%, run 1-1.5ml/hr (0.5-0.75mcg/kg/min). Hemodynamic support 0.25-0.75mcg/kg/min. PPHN 0.3-0.5mcg/kg/min, max 1mcg/kg/min.
Incompatibilities: Frusemide, Imipenem/Cilastatin, Procainamide

name: Morphine 10mg/1ml injection
Dose: Bolus 0.1mg/kg. Infusion: 1mg/kg in 50ml D5%/NS (1ml/hr=20mcg/kg/hr). Usual dose 10-20mcg/kg/hr.
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Cefepime, Micafungin, Phenobarbitone, Phenytoin
Method of administration: Slow bolus over 5 minutes or continuous infusion

name: Naloxone HCl 0.4 mg/1ml injection
Dose: Reversal of opioid respiratory depression: 0.001-0.005mg/kg, up to 0.02mg/kg. Opioid overdose: IV 0.01mg/kg, repeat q2min, then infusion 0.01mg/kg/hr. CONTRAINDICATED in opioid-dependent neonates. DO NOT USE AT DELIVERY if mother suspected/known opioid-dependent.
Incompatibilities: Sodium bicarbonate

name: Netilmicin 150mg/1.5ml injection
Dose: BW<1200g: day0-7 5mg/kg 48h; day8-30 5mg/kg 36h; >30d 5mg/kg 24h. BW1200-2500g: day0-7 5mg/kg 36h; >7d 5mg/kg 24h. Term: day0-7 5mg/kg 24h; 1wk-10y 8mg/kg day1 then 6mg/kg 24h.
Incompatibilities: Ampicillin, Frusemide, Heparin >1u/ml, C-pen, Propofol

name: Noradrenaline 4mg/4ml injection
Dose: Dilution: 0.3mg/kg in 50ml D5%/NS (1ml/hr=0.1mcg/kg/min). Usual range 0.2-2mcg/kg/min. Septic shock 0.2-0.5mcg/kg/min. PPHN with circulatory failure 0.5-1mcg/kg/min.
Incompatibilities: Insulin, Aminophylline, Amphotericin B, Diazepam, Ganciclovir, Phenobarbital, Phenytoin, Sodium bicarbonate, Bactrim

name: Nystatin 100,000 units/ml suspension
Dose: 100,000 unit TDS (not weight-based). Eligible: <1500g with central lines / on broad-spectrum antibiotics / on prolonged steroids (DART regime). Stop: BW<1000g at day28; BW1000-1499g when lines out/antibiotics ceased/3d after off steroids.

name: Pantoprazole 40mg injection
Dose: IV 1mg/kg OD-BD. IV infusion (UGIH) <=40kg: 2mg/kg stat then 0.2mg/kg/hr, max duration 72h.
Incompatibilities: Amphothericin B, Calcium chloride, Caspofungin, Cefepime, Cefotaxime, Ciprofloxacin, Dexamethasone, Diazepam, Dobutamine, Fentanyl, Fluconazole, Lorazepam, Methylprednisolone, Metronidazole, Midazolam, Milrinone, Naloxone, Phenytoin, Ranitidine, Rocuronium, Vancomycin

name: Paracetamol 1000mg/100ml injection
Dose: Analgesia: <32wk 7.5mg/kg 8h. >32wk (<10d old) 7.5mg/kg 6h. >32wk (>10d old) 15mg/kg 6h. PDA closure: 15mg/kg 6h for 5 days.
Incompatibilities: Diazepam, lipids

name: Phenobarbitone 200mg/ml injection
Dose: Loading: IV 20mg/kg, max rate 1mg/kg/min. Additional 10mg/kg at 30min intervals if needed, max cumulative 40mg/kg. Maintenance: 2mg/kg/day (2-8mg/kg), start 24h after loading.
Incompatibilities: Lipids, Hydrocortisone succinate, Insulin, Ranitidine, Vancomycin

name: Phenytoin Sodium 250mg/5ml injection
Dose: Loading: IV 20mg/kg over 30min with cardiac monitoring, may repeat 10-20mg/kg if seizures persist. Maintenance: preterm 2mg/kg 12h; 1st week 3mg/kg 12h; 2wk-4yr 3mg/kg 8h.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Cefepime, Ceftazidime, Clindamycin, Dobutamine, Fentanyl, Heparin, Hydrocortisone, Insulin, Lidocaine, Linezolid, Methadone, Micafungin, Morphine, Phenobarbitone, Potassium chloride, Propofol, Sodium bicarbonate, Vitamin K
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30 minutes, max rate 1-3mg/kg/min

name: Potassium chloride 10% (1g/10ml) injection
Dose: IV max 0.3ml/kg/hr (0.4mmol/kg/hr). Deficit=(Target K-Current K)x0.4xwt(kg). Maintenance 2-4mmol/kg/day. 1mL=1.34mmol K+.
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin B, Diazepam, Phenytoin, lipid, Amoxicillin, Azithromycin, Methylprednisolone, Suxamethonium, Thiopental
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour, DO NOT administer undiluted

name: Rocuronium 50mg/5ml injection
Dose: 0.6-1.2mg/kg IV stat. Infusion 5-15mcg/kg/min (0.3-0.9mg/kg/hr).
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin, Amoxicillin, Azathioprine, Cefazolin, Cloxacillin, Dexamethasone, Diazepam, Erythromycin, Frusemide, Hydrocortisone, Insulin, Lipids, Methylprednisolone, Micafungin, Prednisolone, Thiopental, Trimethoprim, Vancomycin

name: Salbutamol 500mcg/1ml injection
Dose: Acute asthma: Bolus 15mcg/kg over 10min (max 250mcg). Infusion 0.5-1mcg/kg/min up to max 5mcg/kg/min. Hyperkalemia: IV 4mcg/kg single dose over 5min, may repeat. Persistent hyperkalemia infusion 0.3-1mcg/kg/min max.
Incompatibilities: Pantoprazole
Ref: NeoMed, KEMH, Leeds Teaching Hospitals, Paediatric Protocols 4th Ed

name: Sodium benzoate 2g/10ml injection
Dose: Anti-ammonia cocktail: IV 250 mg/kg. Maintenance dose: same dose. Mix with sodium phenylbutyrate & L-arginine in D10% total 50ml infuse over 90 min (33ml/hr); maintenance same dilution over 24 hours.
Incompatibilities: Single line, only mixable with sodium phenylbutyrate & L-arginine
Method of administration: IV infusion via large vein/central line

name: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% w/v injection
Dose: 1ml=1mmol Na+, 1mmol HCO3-. Prescribe as 4.2% (dilute 8.4% 1:1 with WFI). Full correction (4.2%): 0.3 x base excess x weight(kg) x2. Half correction: half of full dose. Continuous infusion max 1mmol/kg/hr. Oral 1-2mmol/kg/day divided.
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, amiodarone, amphothericin B, calcium, cefotaxime, magnesium and phosphate infusions, dobutamine, dopamine, ganciclovir, imipenem-cilastatin, lipid, midazolam, vancomycin, thiopentone, noradrenaline, PN
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30-60 minutes or continuous infusion; avoid simultaneous administration with catecholamines via same line
Ref: Leaflet, NeoFax, South Australian Neonatal Medication Guidelines, Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust

name: Sodium chloride 3% w/v for intravenous infusion
Dose: Content per 1000mL: Sodium 513mmol/L, Chloride 513mmol/L. Osmolarity 1026 mosm/L.

name: Sodium phenylbutyrate 2g/10ml injection
Dose: Anti-ammonia cocktail: IV 250 mg/kg. Maintenance dose: same dose. Mix with sodium benzoate & L-arginine in D10% total 50ml infuse over 90 min. Maintenance: same dilution over 24 hours.
Incompatibilities: Single line, only mixable with sodium benzoate & L-arginine
Method of administration: IV infusion via large vein/central line

name: Sodium valproate 400mg injection
Dose: Status epilepticus: Loading 20mg/kg. Maintenance continuous infusion 1-5mg/kg/hr. Seizure (ANMF): 5mg/kg 12h, increase if required to max 20mg/kg 8-12h.
Incompatibilities: Phenytoin (valproate diluted in NS not compatible with phenytoin)
Method of administration: IV infusion over 60 minutes or continuous infusion

name: Tazobactam & Piperacillin 4.5g (Tazocin) injection
Dose: <=29wk GA: 0-28d 110mg/kg 12h; >28d 110mg/kg 8h. 30-36wk GA: 0-14d 110mg/kg 12h; >14d 110mg/kg 8h. 37-44wk GA: 0-7d 110mg/kg 12h; >7d 110mg/kg 8h. >=45wk GA: 110mg/kg 8h. Infants<6mo 110mg/kg 8h; >6mo 110mg/kg 6h. Dose based on total piperacillin+tazobactam (8:1 ratio).
Incompatibilities: Aminoglycosides, acyclovir, albumin, amiodarone, azithromycin, caspofungin, chlorpromazine, ciprofloxacin, dobutamine, ganciclovir, glycopyrronium bromide, hydralazine, insulin (short-acting), midazolam, pentamidine isetionate, rocuronium, sodium bicarbonate, thiopentone, tranexamic acid, verapamil
Method of administration: IV infusion over at least 60 minutes

name: Thiopentone 500mg injection
Dose: Resistant seizures/status epilepticus: Loading <1mo 2mg/kg; >1mo 4mg/kg. Continuous infusion 1mg/kg/hr, max 8mg/kg/hr.
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, Amiodarone, Azithromycin, Calcium gluconate, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Ertapenem, Frusemide, Ketamine, Leucovorin calcium, Lidocaine, Magnesium, Morphine, Midazolam, Naloxone, Noradrenaline, Tazocin, Rocuronium, Sodium bicarbonate
Method of administration: Via central route only; loading over 10-15 seconds; continuous infusion
Ref: IBM compatibility, South Australian Neonatal Medication Guideline

name: Vancomycin 500mg injection
Dose: General dosing: PMA<29 weeks 15mg/kg 24 hourly. PMA29-35 weeks 15mg/kg 12 hourly. PMA>35 weeks 15mg/kg 8 hourly.
Incompatibilities: Cefazolin, Cefepime, Cefotaxime, Cefoxitin, Ceftazidime, Ceftriaxone, Dexamethasone, Heparin >1u/ml, Phenobarbitone, Tazocin

name: Vasopressin 20 iu/1ml injection
Dose: Hypotension: 0.5unit/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr=0.01unit/kg/hr), range 0.01-0.04 units/kg/hr, titrate q20min. Refractory PPHN: 0.3unit/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr=0.006unit/kg/hr), up to max 0.072unit/kg/hr. DI: starting 0.5mU/kg/hr, usual 0.5-2mU/kg/hr up to 3mU/kg/hr. If serum Na<140, stop vasopressin.
Incompatibilities: Amphoterin B, Diazepam, Frusemide, Phenytoin

name: Vitamin K 1mg/1ml (Phytomenadione) injection
Dose: IV prophylaxis: 0.3mg/kg OD x3 days. IM prophylaxis: BW>=1500g 1mg single dose at birth; BW<1500g 0.5mg single dose at birth. Neonatal cholestasis: 2mg twice weekly up to 2mg OD.
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin (conventional), ampicillin, diazepam, dobutamine, hydralazine, lipid, magnesium sulphate, methylprednisolone, phenytoin, promethazine, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour (Do Not give bolus); intramuscular

name: Trimethoprim 80mg & Sulfamethoxazole 400mg (Co-trimoxazole/ Bactrim) injection
Dose: Stenotrophomonas VAP or bacteremia (off-label): 4 mg/kg (TMP dose) 12 hourly. PCP: 5 mg/kg/dose (TMP dose) 6 hourly for 14-21 days. UTI prophylaxis: 2 mg/kg ON (TMP dose). UTI treatment: 4 mg/kg 12 hourly (TMP dose). AVOID in G6PD deficiency and <1 month old (risk of kernicterus).
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Take required dose and further dilute to 15 times (fluid restriction, central line only) or 25 times.
Storage after reconstitution: 6 hours at RT, DO NOT refrigerate

name: Polymyxin B 500,000 unit (Lyophilized) injection
Dose: Severe, life-threatening, multidrug-resistant infection: IV 20,000 units/kg/dose 12 hourly. Renal adjusted: CrCl>20mL/min 15,000u/kg 12h; CrCl5-20mL/min 10,000u/kg 12h; CrCl<5mL/min 3,000u/kg 12h.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Reconstitute with 5mL WFI to become 500,000 unit/5mL. Withdraw required dose, further dilute with D5% to 1000 unit/mL for administration.
Incompatibilities: Neomycin, Gentamicin, Amikacin, Colistin, Heparin
Method of administration: IV infusion over 60-90 minutes; can infuse over 3 hours if volume is large

name: Aciclovir 250mg injection
Dose: HSV infection (skin/eye/mouth, disseminated, CNS): 20 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency by PMA (preferred, PK-based): PMA<30wk q12h; PMA30-36wk q8h; PMA36-41wk q6h. (Standard/simpler alternative: 20mg/kg q8h all ages.) Duration: skin/eye/mouth 14 days; disseminated or CNS disease 21 days (continue until CSF PCR negative if initially positive at day 19-21). Chronic suppression after IV course: 300mg/m2/dose PO TDS for 6 months. Varicella-zoster with CNS/pulmonary involvement: 10-15mg/kg/dose IV q8h for 5-10 days.
Incompatibilities: Fat emulsion, aztreonam, caffeine citrate, caspofungin, cefepime, dobutamine, dopamine, meropenem, piperacillin-tazobactam
Storage after reconstitution: 12-24h depending on brand, do not refrigerate

name: Ibuprofen 10mg/2ml injection (Pedea)
Dose: PDA closure: 10mg/kg IV/PO, then 5mg/kg at 24h and 48h (standard dose). High-dose option 15-20mg/kg then 7.5-10mg/kg at 24h/48h, particularly for infants >3-5 days old (senior review in extremely preterm). See PDA tab for weight-calculated doses.
Incompatibilities: Do not mix with other drugs in same line

name: Indometacin (Indomethacin) 1mg injection
Dose: PDA closure, age-based 3-dose course: <48h 0.2/0.1/0.1 mg/kg; 2-7 days 0.2/0.2/0.2 mg/kg; >7 days 0.2/0.25/0.25 mg/kg, given 12-24 hourly (24h as local default). Withhold subsequent dose if urine output <0.6mL/kg/h until renal function recovers. See PDA tab for weight-calculated doses.
Diluent: Preservative-free NS or WFI per product; do not further dilute after reconstitution per manufacturer
Incompatibilities: Do not mix with other drugs in same line

name: Sildenafil 10mg/ml oral suspension
Dose: PPHN: 0.5 mg/kg/dose PO q6h; if inadequate response, may increase up to max 2 mg/kg/dose. Stop after 6-8 doses if no improvement; reduce/stop if significant hypotension develops. See PPHN tab for weight-calculated doses.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Commercial oral suspension; shake well before use

name: Frusemide (Furosemide) 20mg/2ml injection
Dose: IV 0.5-1 mg/kg/dose, 6-24 hourly (titrate to response). IV infusion alternative: 0.1-0.4 mg/kg/hour.
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Caffeine, Caspofungin, Ciprofloxacin, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Fluconazole, Gentamicin, Hydralazine, Metoclopramide, Midazolam, Milrinone, Netilmicin, Nicardipine, Vancomycin, Vasopressin

name: Frusemide (Furosemide) 10mg/ml oral solution
Dose: 0.5-1 mg/kg, 6-24 hourly.

name: Sodium glycerophosphate (Glycophos) 20mmol/20ml injection
Dose: Phosphate supplementation: 1-1.5 mmol/kg/day IV (preterm growing infant up to 1.6-3.5mmol/kg/day). 1mL Glycophos = 1mmol phosphate + 2mmol sodium.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dilute in WFI or NS; peripheral line max concentration 0.1mmol/mL, central line max 0.4mmol/mL
Incompatibilities: Solutions containing magnesium or calcium (e.g. Hartmann's, Ringer's, Plasmalyte), TPN

name: Phosphate Sandoz effervescent tablet (oral)
Dose: 1-2 mmol/kg/day phosphate, divided with feeds. Each tablet: 16.1mmol phosphate, 20.4mmol sodium, 3.1mmol potassium. Separate from calcium supplements by ≥1 hour.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dissolve tablet in water per unit dilution protocol before dosing

name: Potassium chloride 1g/10ml oral solution
Dose: Maintenance/correction for hypokalaemia: 2-4 mmol/kg/day, divided 3 doses. Deficit (mmol) = (target K - current K) x 0.4 x weight(kg). 1mL = 1.34 mmol K+.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Reconstitute powder with WFI per product; shake well before use

name: Calcium carbonate 500mg tablet (oral)
Dose: Hypocalcaemia: total elemental calcium intake 120-200 mg/kg/day from all sources, or ward practice 50mg elemental calcium (quarter tablet) q6-8h. 1 tablet = 200mg elemental calcium = 5mmol Ca.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare; solution will be cloudy, tablet may not fully dissolve. Avoid combining with phosphate/iron/EBM+HMF in the same dose.
Method of administration: Separate from phosphate, iron, thyroxine, phenytoin by ≥2 hours; serve with feeding, not mixed into milk syringe
Ref: KEMH & Perth Children's Hospital, SGH formulary

name: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 1000iu capsule
Dose: Treatment of Vitamin D deficiency (first 3 months): <3mo 1000-2000 IU OD; 3-12mo 2000 IU OD. Routine preterm supplementation: 400 IU OD (unit-dependent — confirm local protocol).
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare
Ref: Global Consensus on Nutritional Rickets 2016, NeoFax, SGH formulary

name: Iron Polymaltose complex [10mg elemental iron/mL]
Dose: Prophylaxis/treatment: elemental iron 6 mg/kg OD, typically starting ~day 14 of life once feeds established.

name: Folic acid 1mg/ml oral solution
Dose: Fixed dose 0.1mg OD during admission; upon discharge increase to 0.5mg OD. 1mg=1mL.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded; shake well before use

name: Multivitamin drops
Dose: Up to 1 year old: 0.5mL BD. Upon discharge: 1mL OD.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Commercial product, shake well before use

name: Micafungin sodium 50mg injection
Dose: Invasive/systemic candidiasis: neonates & infants <4 months 10 mg/kg IV OD (up to 15mg/kg/day reported for extremely premature infants or resistant strains — confirm with ID/pharmacy); infants >4 months 4 mg/kg IV OD.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Reconstitute with 5mL NS to 50mg/5mL; dilute further to final concentration 0.5-1.5mg/mL (central line if 1.6-4mg/mL)
Incompatibilities: Albumin, Amiodarone, Dobutamine, Adrenaline, Insulin, Levofloxacin, Midazolam, Morphine, Phenytoin, Rocuronium
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour, protect from light during infusion

name: Linezolid 2mg/ml injection
Dose: Selected resistant Gram-positive infections (e.g. MRSA not responding to vancomycin): 10 mg/kg/dose IV/PO TDS (infants and children <12 years).

name: Enoxaparin 20mg/0.2ml injection
Dose: Prophylaxis: SC 0.75 mg/kg/dose q12h. Treatment: preterm 1.5-2 mg/kg/dose q12h; term 1.5-1.7 mg/kg/dose q12h. Adjust to anti-Xa level (target range per local lab). Duration typically 6 weeks-3 months depending on thrombus site/response.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dilute pre-filled syringe with NS to 20mg/1mL (1mg/0.05mL) for accurate small-volume dosing

name: Tranexamic acid 500mg/5ml injection
Dose: Major bleeding/haemorrhage: 10-15 mg/kg/dose IV, 8 hourly.
Method of administration: Slow IV over 5-10 minutes — do not exceed 1mL/min (hypotension risk if too fast)

name: Sucrose 24% oral solution
Dose: Procedural analgesia: 0.5-1mL, given 2 minutes before a painful procedure (e.g. heel prick, venepuncture, IM injection).
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Add WFI to bottle per product to reconstitute

name: Lidocaine 25mg & Prilocaine 25mg cream (EMLA)
Dose: Topical local anaesthesia for procedures (PICC, LP, venepuncture): 0.5-1g applied 30-60 minutes before procedure. NOT recommended for preterm infants <37 weeks GA — risk of methaemoglobinaemia.
Method of administration: Apply topically under occlusive dressing, remove before procedure

name: Digoxin 500mcg/2ml injection
Dose: Consult paediatric cardiologist before initiating. Loading: 15mcg/kg stat, then 5mcg/kg after 6h, then maintenance 3-5mcg/kg q12h (max 200mcg IV/250mcg oral). Reduce dose ~20-25% when switching oral→IV. Renal impairment: reduce dose by ≥50%.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dilute to at least 4-fold volume with diluent to avoid precipitation; max concentration 62.5mcg/mL
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, Amiodarone, Caspofungin, Dobutamine, Fluconazole, Propofol
Method of administration: IV over 30-60 minutes; TDM level 12-24h after loading dose (pre-dose level)

name: Tobramycin injection
Dose: Gram-negative infection (alternative aminoglycoside): dosing similar structure to Gentamicin — 4-5mg/kg/dose, extended-interval by current PMA (see Gentamicin entry/Sepsis tab pattern as a guide). Confirm local frequency chart before use — less commonly stocked than gentamicin/amikacin at this unit.

name: Ganciclovir sodium 500mg/10ml injection
Dose: Symptomatic congenital CMV infection: 6 mg/kg/dose IV q12h for minimum 6 weeks, then transition to oral valganciclovir to complete 6 months total treatment where possible. CYTOTOXIC drug.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Prepared by cytotoxic drug reconstitution service only
Incompatibilities: Lipid, Cefepime, Piperacillin/Tazobactam
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour, flush before/after with NS

name: Valganciclovir 50mg/ml oral syrup
Dose: Congenital CMV infection treatment (step-down from IV ganciclovir, or primary oral treatment): 16 mg/kg/dose PO q12h for 6 months total. CYTOTOXIC drug.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Commercial or CDR-pharmacy compounded; requires ≥1 day advance notice; shake well before use

name: Human immunoglobulin (IVIG) 5g/50ml (10%) injection
Dose: ITP: 0.4 g/kg/day for 2-5 days, OR 1 g/kg/day for 1-2 days. Isoimmune haemolytic disease (Rh incompatibility, ≥35wk GA): 0.5-1 g/kg once over 2h, may repeat at 12h. Sepsis (adjunct): 0.5-1 g/kg/day OD for 1-3 days.
Incompatibilities: Single line, do not mix with other medications
Method of administration: IV infusion, typically over 10 hours — follow unit IVIG infusion protocol

name: Levothyroxine (L-thyroxine) 25mcg & 50mcg tablet
Dose: Congenital hypothyroidism, by FT4 severity: subclinical 5-10mcg/kg/dose OD; mild (FT4>10) 10mcg/kg/dose OD; moderate (FT4 5-10) 10mcg/kg/dose OD; severe (FT4<5) 15mcg/kg/dose OD.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare each dose; note two strengths available (25 & 50mcg) — check carefully
Ref: Consensus Guidelines on Congenital Hypothyroidism Malaysia, UpToDate

name: Spironolactone 25mg tablet
Dose: Chronic lung disease / cardiac failure (diuretic-sparing): 3.125mg/dose OD or BD (fixed dose, not weight-based in this unit's practice — confirm against current weight-based alternative if preferred).
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded to 2.5mg/mL

name: Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg tablet
Dose: Chronic lung disease (often with spironolactone), or with Diazoxide for hypoglycaemia (offsets fluid retention): 1-1.5 mg/kg, 12-24 hourly.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded to 5mg/mL; give morning dose as early as possible

name: Ursodeoxycholic acid 250mg capsule
Dose: Neonatal cholestasis: 10-15 mg/kg/dose, 12 hourly.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded to 50mg/mL

name: Zinc 15mg, B6, Vitamin A tablet
Dose: 1 mg/kg/day elemental zinc, up to 1 tablet OD. Each tablet ≈ 14.9mg elemental zinc.

name: Vitamin E (Tocopherol) oral drops
Dose: Preterm supplementation: 40 units (2 drops) OD (not weight-based).

name: Vitamin A oral/IM injection
Dose: BPD-prevention regimen (where used): 5000 IU IM, 3 times weekly for 4 weeks. (Distinct from the high-dose measles/high-risk single-dose regimen — confirm indication before dosing.)
Ref: NeoFax, ANMF — confirm local regimen before use

name: Erythropoietin (Epoetin alfa) injection
Dose: Anaemia of prematurity (only if unit protocol uses EPO): 200-250 units/kg SC/IV, 3 times weekly. Ensure adequate iron supplementation concurrently. Confirm local protocol/indication before starting — not all units use routine EPO.
